core.signatureMove: Neutral lattice: structure from spacing steps and declared props, never from decoration.

rules.name: One Primary Per Region
rules.statement: Give each region one primary button and label every button with a verb.
rules.why: Two primaries ask the reader to guess which action matters; a noun label hides what pressing does.

rules.name: Cards Earn Their Keep
rules.statement: A card groups one topic. Never nest cards, and never wrap every section in one.
rules.why: Containers inside containers add depth and noise; spacing and headings already group content.

rules.name: Steps, Not Pixels
rules.statement: Set layout with declared props and token spacing steps; never write pixel values.
rules.why: Tokens keep every system and theme coherent; pixel values pin one rendering.

rules.name: Bind, Don't Copy
rules.statement: Feed numbers and text from data and state with expressions instead of retyping them.
rules.why: A retyped figure drifts from its source and cannot respond to filters.

rules.name: Navigation Fits The Shape
rules.statement: Use a sidebar for 3–9 persistent sections and tabs for 2–6 sibling views; omit both when the page reads straight through.
rules.why: Navigation is optional; extra chrome on a short page costs more than it helps.

rules.name: Wire Every Control
rules.statement: Every button, form and modal needs a handler or a command that reaches it.
rules.why: A control that does nothing teaches readers the page is broken.

rules.name: Describe The Picture
rules.statement: Give every image alt text and every chart a label that states what it shows.
rules.why: Assistive technology and screenshots depend on the label; a bare chart says nothing to them.

ledger.signatureMove: Dense, square and mono: every panel is an addressable ticker.

rules.name: Short Uppercase Labels
rules.statement: Keep tab labels under 15 characters and write button labels that still read in uppercase.
rules.why: Ledger uppercases labels in a narrow mono face; long sentence-case text truncates or shouts.

rules.name: Segmented Choices Stay Short
rules.statement: Use the dropdown for up to six short options; pin core/dropdown@1 for long or dynamic lists.
rules.why: Ledger shows every option at once as a segmented control, so a long list overflows the row.

rules.name: Panels Sit Flush
rules.statement: Fill a card edge to edge and give it a short panel code such as PNL-01.
rules.why: Dense grids depend on bodies sitting flush; padding-heavy content breaks the rhythm.

rules.name: Trends Carry Data
rules.statement: Add a stat trend only with 8–30 real numbers behind it.
rules.why: A sparkline with no data is decoration, and in a dense tool it reads as a measurement.

rules.name: Group The Navigation
rules.statement: Group sidebar items under headers, keep labels to one line and use 2–4 character codes.
rules.why: Ledger truncates at one line; groups and tickers keep a long list scannable.

atelier.signatureMove: Soft and editorial: one story at a time, set in serif with room to breathe.

rules.name: Short Navigation
rules.statement: Keep the sidebar to six items, each with a one-line description; leave dense tool navigation to Ledger.
rules.why: Atelier is for reading and storytelling; a long menu turns a story into a tool.

rules.name: Four Tabs At Most
rules.statement: Switch between two to four views with pill tabs and never add a fifth.
rules.why: The pill switcher is built for a few friendly choices; more belongs in a page of sections.

rules.name: Friendly Choices
rules.statement: Offer two to ten options of up to three words each.
rules.why: Options render as wrapping chips, and long labels turn them into a wall of text.

rules.name: One Primary Per Card
rules.statement: Put at most one primary pill button in a card; the rest are secondary or quiet.
rules.why: The ink-filled primary is the page's one loud gesture.

rules.name: Captions In Sentences
rules.statement: Show up to three stats per row, each with a caption written as a sentence.
rules.why: A big serif figure needs a sentence of context; a fourth stat crowds the row.

rules.name: Tables Leave The Card
rules.statement: Keep tables out of cards when the page must work on a narrow screen.
rules.why: Atelier cards are padded and soft, so a table inside one overflows on phones.
